# M0-S3: the compiler rejects a package that mixes user-authored .go
# and .lgo files with correctness::mixed_package. A pure .lgo package
# compiles, and compiler-generated cgo outputs beside .lgo files are
# exempt from the check.

env GOPROXY=off

# Mixing a.go and b.lgo fails and names both file classes.
# The compiler prints its diagnostics on stdout.
! go tool compile -p p -o $WORK/p.o a.go b.lgo
stdout '\[correctness::mixed_package\] cannot mix \.go files \(a\.go\) and \.lgo files \(b\.lgo\) in one package'

# Several files per class are listed sorted by base name, and alias
# extensions, with or without a trailing U+FE0F, count as loGo/s files.
! go tool compile -p p -o $WORK/s.o z.go a.go c.lgo b.⚡ e.⚡️
stdout '\[correctness::mixed_package\] cannot mix \.go files \(a\.go, z\.go\) and \.lgo files \(b\.⚡, c\.lgo, e\.⚡️\) in one package'

# Two .lgo files compile.
go tool compile -p p -o $WORK/q.o c.lgo d.lgo

# Cgo outputs beside an .lgo file are exempt and compile.
go tool compile -p p -o $WORK/r.o e.lgo _cgo_gotypes.go x.cgo1.go

-- a.go --
package p

func A() int { return 1 }

-- b.lgo --
package p

func B() int { return 2 }

-- c.lgo --
package p

func C() int { return 3 }

-- d.lgo --
package p

func D() int { return 4 }

-- e.lgo --
package p

func E() int { return 5 }

-- z.go --
package p

func Z() int { return 26 }

-- b.⚡ --
package p

func Bz() int { return 7 }

-- e.⚡️ --
package p

func Ez() int { return 8 }

-- x.cgo1.go --
package p

func X() int { return 9 }

-- _cgo_gotypes.go --
package p

func CgoTypes() int { return 6 }
